jobs.title: Head of Tokenization
jobs.description_text:
We are seeking a senior Product leader to drive our strategic expansion from crypto-assets into all tokenized assets so the Talos platform has front-to-back support for tokenized equities, bonds and other emerging asset classes on-chain. You will own this strategic initiative, working closely with the Head of Product Strategy and other product managers to drive go-to-market strategy; client and partner engagement; and setting overall project delivery direction. This position is ultimately accountable for P&L in a new product line.
 
Responsibilities
 
Lead specification, high-level design and delivery of a full tokenized securities venue platform and its integration into Talos, inclusive of all key elements
Market structure
Liquidity provision, clearing & settlement
On-chain vs. off-chain integrations
Identity and KYC/AML
Regulatory reporting
Direct technical product management and Engineering, both dedicated project resources and cross-team dependencies, to ensure rapid, coordinated delivery of the new product
Develop and own relationships with early design partners & ecosystem partners to iteratively shape product requirements, and drive key build/buy/partner decisions
Work with Revenue on go-to-market strategy, materials, marketing and own product line P&L
Work with Legal & Compliance to ensure regulatory compliance across jurisdictions, and help identify opportunities coming out of emerging regulatory directions worldwide
Qualifications
 
At least 15 years of professional experience
Experience leading complex capital markets technology projects at banks, brokerages, asset managers, fintechs or FMIs
Demonstrated track record of product ownership working with internal and external stakeholders
Deep knowledge of capital markets across the life of the trade trading, financing, risk management and trading controls, clearing and settlement, etc.) and ability to think critically about what changes and what stays the same with tokenized assets
Experience developing crypto or tokenized asset trading, portfolio, clearing & settlement products and demonstrated knowledge of blockchain networks and DeFi
Effective collaboration cross-functionally and cross-product to drive project success in a fast-changing environment

jobs.title: Legal Engineer - In-House
jobs.description_text:
About Us
Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.
Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.
2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to
 $200M+ in ARR
, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.
We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.
Joining Legora means three things.
We 
lean in: 
ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.
We 
fight for excellence:
 high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.
We
 grow together:
 as a team and with our customers.
Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.
If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.
What you'll do
Let's get the tricky part out of the way: this role doesn't fit neatly into a box. It's part legal ops, part product specialist, part solutions architect, and part trusted advisor. If you want a role that stays static, this isn't it.
Your mission is to help some of the world's leading in-house legal teams get the absolute most out of Legora. You'll understand how legal teams operate inside complex businesses, identify where AI can make the biggest difference, and turn that potential into workflows that deliver real value.
You'll be the person clients call when they want to rethink how their legal function works — whether that's transforming a high-volume process, embedding Legora across a global team, or building the case for AI with senior stakeholders.
Specifically, you will
Act as a genuine thought partner to in-house legal teams — understanding their business, priorities and constraints, then identifying high-value opportunities to transform how legal work gets done.
Own the journey alongside Customer Success from early pilots through onboarding to enterprise-wide adoption, turning initial use cases into sustained, measurable impact across the legal function.
Design and implement workflows around the realities of in-house legal work — from contracts and commercial advisory to regulatory, compliance, disputes and knowledge management.
Partner with General Counsel, legal operations leaders and legal teams to build the case for AI adoption, connecting Legora's capabilities to the outcomes that matter to their business.
Be the voice of the in-house lawyer inside Legora — bringing a deep understanding of their needs, constraints and workflows into product development, roadmap priorities and strategic direction.
Deliver clear, confident product demos, workshops and training that make the potential of Legora tangible for everyone from individual lawyers to legal leadership.
Help clients navigate one of the most significant shifts in how in-house legal teams operate — moving beyond individual productivity gains towards fundamental changes in how legal services are delivered to the business.
Document what works, build scalable playbooks and help shape how Legora serves corporate legal teams as we grow globally.
What you'll bring
You've worked inside an in-house legal team and understand the reality of being a lawyer within a business. You know that great in-house legal work isn't just about giving the right legal answer — it's about balancing risk, commercial priorities, speed and the needs of stakeholders across the organisation.

jobs.title: Director of Data Products
jobs.description_text:
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.
We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.
Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.
In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.
But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output.
Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.
Why this role
Every one of Multiverse's 800+ employees needs data to do their job well, and in the AI era - our ability to leverage data is more important than ever!
As Director of Data Products, you will own the platform, the products, the tools, the processes and the self-serve layer, so that the answer arrives before the request does.
You will be a force-multiplier for the quality, velocity and impact of Multiverse's decision making, and a driving force behind how data and AI are leveraged across the entire business. You will ensure that how we interact with data and deliver data products fully realises the potential of AI.
You will sit in the Data & Insight leadership team, reporting to our VP of Data & Insight, with a seat in company-wide planning and governance forums. You will manage 8 analytics engineers and developers within a wider team of ~20, collaborating with senior stakeholders across the org to coordinate a complex set of competing needs.
What you'll own
Data leverage across Multiverse
The platform, products and self-serve layer that ~800 people use to find, understand and act on our data — reducing the dependency on Data & Insight to answer questions others could answer themselves.
Direction on tooling: evaluate the options, make the call, take the organisation through the change.
Curation of our semantic layer so it covers Multiverse's core business concepts, data and metrics — with clear ownership and stewardship agreed with Domain D&I Leads and business stakeholders, and core architecture aligned with the Director of Data Engineering.
Governance embedded through the platform itself — quality, definitions, stewardship, access — so that trust and speed stop being a trade-off.
Real adoption, through documentation, training and support that reaches every relevant domain. Optimising the user experience alongside secure controls and seamless interconnectivity (APIs, MCPs).
Cross-functional roadmap delivery
D&I's operational planning process: around 50 quarterly projects properly scoped, clearly defined and appropriately resourced, with capacity reallocated as priorities move.
Representation of D&I in company-wide planning and governance forums, bringing a data lens to decisions being made elsewhere in the business.
A roadmap that reflects genuine business priority rather than the loudest request, with data needs surfaced early.
Progress against milestones — risks identified ahead of time, blockers raised, solutions coordinated.
Operational excellence
Driving the team's cycle planning, standups and retrospectives, run so they are genuinely useful and action-oriented.
Standards, playbooks and best practice for how work is scoped, how handoffs happen and how outputs are documented — with AI embedded where it creates real leverage.
Fair triage of inbound support and feature requests, and an escalation route for issues that cross domain boundaries.
D&I's own operational metrics — project velocity, support throughput, self-ser
